szoveg_eredeti:
Generative AI is transforming science, industry, and society while raising urgent questions about governance and public participation.

Artificial intelligence has moved from a specialised technology to an everyday reality for millions of people. According to the latest report from the One Hundred Year Study on Artificial Intelligence (AI100), the past five years have marked a watershed moment in AI's development, driven by advances in large-scale computing, vast datasets, and the rapid rise of generative AI. The report, AI Goes Mainstream: The Scaling Era and the Rise of Generative AI, was released by AI100, a longitudinal project administered by Stanford University's Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI). Published every five years, the study examines AI's development and its impact on people, communities, and society across technical, ethical, economic, and societal domains.

Among the members of the 2026 AI100 Study Panel was Iyad Rahwan, Director of the Center for Human and Machines at the Max Planck Institute for Human Development. The international panel brought together experts from computer science, philosophy, sociology, and related disciplines to assess how AI has evolved since the previous report in 2021.

The 2026 AI100 report examines the scaling of data and computing resources behind generative AI, advances in scientific discovery, investment in AI infrastructure, the concentration of frontier AI development, cybersecurity and military applications, the trustworthiness of digital media, emerging risks, public participation, and international governance.

“The 2021 AI100 report was very optimistic about the potential for rapid AI progress. What we did not foresee was the ‘ChatGPT moment’ that took the world by storm. AI suddenly became a mainstream topic, and today billions of people interact with AI on a regular basis. This shift has fundamentally changed how society, business, and industry view the technology,” says Iyad Rahwan, member of the 2026 AI100 Study Panel.

The latest AI100 report builds on previous editions from 2016 and 2021 and documents how artificial intelligence has evolved from a specialised research technology into a pervasive social force. It responds to 12 standing questions about AI’s advances, opportunities, dangers, and societal effects, includes deep dives into AI geopolitics and the scaling era, and compares developments since 2021 with the previous panel’s assessments.

For the researchers on the Study Panel, one thing is clear: The coming years will be decisive in shaping the opportunities and risks of this technology.

Launched in 2014, the One-Hundred-Year Study on Artificial Intelligence (AI100) is a longitudinal project led by an international Standing Committee of AI experts and administered out of Stanford’s Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI). Every five years, AI100 convenes a Study Panel to assess AI’s progress and its influences on people, communities, and society across technical, ethical, economic, and societal domains. Learn more at ai100.stanford.edu.

More information: https://ai100.stanford.edu
